purpose: Phase 0B isolated-worker timeout and concurrent-cold-build evidence for the OpenTitan Slang workload; this is a benchmark receipt, not a production worker, cache, or single-flight implementation.

two_worker_concurrency.method: Start two independent one-sample OpenTitan spike parents in one shell, wait for both, and measure the shell with GNU time. Both frontend workers use separate processes and overlap in wall time.

overall.child_status_interpretation: Both children emitted valid blocked feasibility results because the same 65 frontend diagnostics remain; neither crashed or timed out.

current_semantic_projection.difference_excluded_from_semantic_identi: symbols_by_kind.Variable aggregate was 319721 versus 319762; exact diagnostics, tops, definitions, instance count, and oracle memberships matched.
current_semantic_projection.policy: Aggregate frontend visitor counts remain reported facts but are not connectivity or cache identity.

memory_interpretation.sum_is: a conservative inferred bound, not a sampled aggregate process-tree peak
memory_interpretation.overlap_evidence: Overall 55.51s wall is approximately one worker wall, while user+system CPU is approximately the sum of both workers.

decision.default_cold_build_admission: one active cold frontend build per TraceWeave server until Phase 1 implements memory-aware single-flight/resource admission
reasons: A native frontend needs hard timeout and crash containment.
The measured large workload peaks near 2.14 GiB RSS per worker.
A two-worker run overlaps successfully but requires a conservative combined memory budget near 4.27 GiB.
A thread cannot reclaim a crashed or wedged native frontend or release its process RSS independently.
decision.persistent_warm_worker_policy: No persistent worker or cache is implemented in Phase 0B. Fresh-process samples with uncontrolled OS page cache must not be labeled cache hits; persistent-worker/cache behavior is a Phase 1 acceptance measurement.
